analysis: What changed vs the 4:00 AM brief: the overnight story broadened from memory chips to the whole AI-infrastructure stack. Vertiv's Q3 blowout (revenue +60.8% year over year, EPS $2.21 vs $1.82 expected, plus a Q4 guide above consensus) and GE Vernova's beat-and-raise (orders up 96% to $29B, 2026 guidance lifted) confirm the demand side that SK Hynix flagged hours earlier — power and cooling are now printing the same AI-demand evidence as memory. The second new thread is energy: a Houthi missile claim against Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery, unconfirmed by Saudi authorities, pushed Brent toward $116 and WTI back above $101, which is the mirror image of Tuesday's oil slide that had eased inflation jitters. That keeps the 10-year pinned just above 5% into the Fed decision and makes the 10:30 a.m. ET EIA inventory report a live input, not background. Signal: AI-infrastructure earnings are beating across memory, power and cooling in the same 24 hours — the tape's engine has breadth beyond chips. Noise: single-stock premarket percentages, the still-unconfirmed OpenAI-TPU report, and any read of the Fed decision itself — a hold is priced at roughly 91-96%, so Warsh's December guidance is the only part that can move markets.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures mixed into the open: Nasdaq 100 futures +0.5%, S&P 500 futures +0.1%, Dow futures -0.2% in recent trading, per Investopedia; the 10-year yield sits above 5.01%, up 1 bp from Tuesday's close.
headlines.why_it_matters: Same tech-led split as the 4 AM read — Nasdaq strength against a soft Dow — with yields still parked just above 5% into the Fed decision.

headlines.headline: Vertiv crushed Q3: non-GAAP EPS $2.21 beat the $1.82 consensus by $0.39, revenue $4.31B (+60.8% year over year) beat by $550M, and Q4 guidance calls for $4,413M in net sales vs $4.31B consensus with 50% organic growth; shares rose about 16% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cooling and power for data centers is beating by the same wide margins as memory — a second, independent confirmation that AI-infrastructure demand is still accelerating.

headlines.headline: GE Vernova beat and raised: Q3 EPS $4.81 vs $4.01 expected, revenue $12.64B vs $12B, orders up 96% year over year to $29B; 2026 guidance lifted to about $47B in sales and about $6.6B EBITDA, plus a $9B deal to acquire grid-equipment maker Trench Group. Shares dipped initially, then recovered to about +2.5% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: A raised guide on a near-doubling of orders extends the AI-power-demand story from chips into the grid — and the early dip-then-recovery shows buyers stepping in even after a big run.

headlines.headline: Oil jumped after Yemen's Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery (550,000 barrels per day) with a missile; Saudi authorities had not confirmed the strike. Brent rose 1.8% to $115.90 and WTI 2.0% to $101.91 as of 0735 GMT. API data showed crude stocks fell 2.03M barrels in the week ended Oct 23, versus analyst expectations of a small build; the official EIA report lands at 10:30 a.m. ET today.
headlines.why_it_matters: A supply-risk premium is back in crude hours before the Fed decision — higher oil feeds the inflation backdrop Warsh will be asked about, and it reverses Tuesday's oil slide that had calmed sentiment.

headlines.headline: Alphabet rose about 1.5% premarket ahead of its Q3 print after the close (consensus roughly $128B revenue, about $2.94-3.03 EPS, Google Cloud near $29.15B); the OpenAI-TPU purchase report remains unconfirmed by either company.
headlines.why_it_matters: Alphabet is the premarket Mag 7 leader into its own earnings — the unconfirmed TPU report is still just a sentiment lift, so the print itself has to do the work.

headlines.headline: Microsoft edged lower premarket ahead of fiscal Q1 after the close (consensus roughly $90.6B revenue, about $4.71-4.73 EPS, Azure growth near 44.8% with roughly 27 points from AI services).
headlines.why_it_matters: A flat-to-down premarket into the print means the bar is Azure growth and capex commentary, not the headline EPS — the same strict grading that hit Tuesday's reporters.

headlines.headline: Megacap premarket snapshot (07:53 ET): Nvidia +0.88%, Tesla +0.69%, Apple -0.35%, Microsoft -0.37%; Tesla extends Tuesday's Mag 7-leading +4.04% session and its October rally, the month's best among the group.
headlines.why_it_matters: Chips and Tesla are carrying the premarket while Apple and Microsoft sit flat — narrow leadership into a day with two market-moving events.

headlines.headline: The Fed decision lands at 2:00 p.m. ET with Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET; markets price only about a 9% chance of a hike this week per CME FedWatch, while December hike odds sit near 75%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hold is priced in, so the trade is December guidance — a hawkish steer with the 10-year above 5% and oil back over $101 would hit the AI trade's financing story hardest.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: Boeing fell 11% Tuesday, its worst day since the pandemic-era lows, after another quarterly loss, weighing on the Dow even as the S&P rose 0.60% and the Nasdaq 1.18%; Tuesday's breadth was narrow, with most S&P 500 stocks closing lower despite the index gain.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tuesday's gain was big-tech-led, not broad — a reminder that today's tape can stay green on the indexes while most stocks lag.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. The Q3 distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized, ~8.4% yield) pays Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26. Q3 earnings arrive before the open Tue Nov 3 with an 11 a.m. ET call. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. Background: on Oct 1 the partnership issued 34.5M non-convertible Class A units at a fixed 9.25% annual distribution rate in an internal reorganization, and it now trades on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) after moving from NYSE on Oct 5. WTI back above $101 on the Saudi refinery headlines keeps the energy backdrop supportive with no company-specific catalyst.
